items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training
Advanced experience with planning for real-world deployment and creation of qualitative and quantitative feedback mechanisms across an interdisciplinary team.

Experience designing and building software, tooling, or infrastructure for agentic AI / LLM systems such as agent frameworks, tool and skill integrations, or evaluation harnesses, with a particular focus on the Researcher Experience and human-agent interaction patterns.

Experience participating in multi-stakeholder open source communities: distributed decision making, navigating uncertainty, building consensus, coordinating paid and volunteer contributors, mentoring new members.
Experience reviewing code through open discussion and iterations on GitHub. Demonstrated track record using issues and pull requests (or similar) for transparent and distributed project management.
Experience conducting research in a data-intensive scientific domain in academia or industry.
Applies advanced software
concepts to plan, design, develop, modify, debug, deploy, and evaluate highly complex interface, software and/or infrastructure solutions
that enable agentic AI systems to produce reproducible scientific research

Works with domain scientists to identify friction in their research workflows. Conducts hands-on user research and usability testing, and translates findings into software requirements across literature search, analysis execution and review, and preparation of results for publication.
Analyzes existing highly complex open source software or works to design and implement
interaction patterns for agent-assisted research. Establishes reusable frontend components, interaction principles, and visual language for these workflows
. Understands and applies industry practices, open source community standards and department policies and procedures in depth.

10% Prepares and approves or obtains approval for user and developer documentation. Initiates and oversees changes in development, maintenance and system standards. Sets the technical requirements for software specifications, engaging across open source communities as appropriate. Communicates technical requirements to interdisciplinary experts and trainees with varied technical expertise.
10% Contributes to and supports the maintenance and sustainability of
projects. Maintenance can include issue triage, code and documentation review, contributing new features, mentoring new contributors, continuous integration testing, and release management.
10% Develops project plans as part of an interdisciplinary team, delivers allocated tasks, and communicates progress regularly.
5% Stays up to date on applicable research and software engineering standards, including applications of agentic AI for science (new models and tools, agentic architectures, and evaluation methods),

and security and accessibility practices. Implements cutting edge practices into software and protocol standards, meeting UC Berkeley-specific policy requirements and national and international standards as applicable.
5% Serves as technical lead for one or two software
development projects of moderate to broad scope. Meets with interdisciplinary project teams and provides regular updates on progress.
5% Advances the work of the UC Berkeley Open Source Program Office (OSPO) by demonstrating the value and impact of open source practices.
Demonstrated fluency using agentic AI and large language model (LLM) coding agents (such as Claude and/or Codex) to move quickly between design, prototyping, and implementation.

Proven track record building or designing tools that are used by research teams to conduct cutting-edge innovation in the life sciences, physical sciences (astronomy, physics, chemistry), and geosciences, and/or the social sciences, humanities, and public health.

A curious mindset and appetite for navigating complexity and uncertainty. A track record of scoping and delivering on requirements from interdisciplinary teams of domain experts and trainees with varied technical expertise.
Self-motivated and works independently and as part of a team. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines.
Advanced programming skills, including Python expertise.
Strong visual and interaction design craft, including the ability to establish interaction principles, reusable components, and a coherent visual language for deeply technical software.
Demonstrated software development and maintenance skills: version control with git, testing, continuous integration and/or continuous deployment with GitHub Actions or similar.
Advanced skills associated with software specification, design, modification, implementation and deployment of large-scale, user-facing systems.
Excellent project leadership and management skills.
Demonstrated ability to understand functional needs and how systems can support those needs, particularly in the context of leveraging existing functionality in scientific open source libraries.

Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization and at academic and industry conferences.
Demonstrated complex problem-solving skills.
